title: Authentication and Authorization

header.html: Implement identity federation (2.1.1); implement access control with fine-grained permissions, security tokens and MFA (2.1.2); configure programmatic access (2.1.3); use presigned URLs (2.1.4); make authenticated calls (2.1.5); define permissions for IAM principals and resources (2.1.6); assume an IAM role (2.1.7)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 2.1

html:
1IAM in one page

Concept Meaning
Principal Who is acting: a user, role or service
Identity-based policy Attached to a user, group or role: what it can do
Resource-based policy Attached to a resource (S3 bucket, SQS queue, KMS key, Lambda): who may use it
Trust policy Part of a role: who may assume it
Least privilege Grant only the actions and resources needed
Explicit deny A deny always wins over any allow

A role has no long-term credentials; whoever assumes it gets temporary credentials.

Exam tip

. Default is deny. Explicit deny beats allow. Cross-account access needs both sides to allow (identity policy and resource policy or trust).

2AWS STS and assuming roles

AWS STS issues temporary security credentials (access key, secret key, session token) that expire.

Call Use
AssumeRole An IAM principal takes a role (including cross-account)
AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity A user authenticated by a web identity provider (OIDC) gets a role
AssumeRoleWithSAML A user from a SAML identity provider gets a role

MFA can be required in a policy condition (for example, aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent) before a sensitive action.

3Amazon Cognito and federation

Component Purpose
User pool A user directory: sign-up, sign-in, MFA, returns JWT tokens (ID, access, refresh); can federate with social and enterprise identity providers
Identity pool Exchanges identities (from a user pool or other provider) for temporary AWS credentials to call AWS services directly

Exam tip

. "Users sign in to my app" = user pool. "App users need AWS credentials to call S3 or DynamoDB" = identity pool. API Gateway can use a Cognito authorizer with a user pool token.

Identity federation lets users sign in with an external identity (a corporate directory through SAML, a social login through OIDC) and receive temporary AWS access without creating IAM users.

4Programmatic access and presigned URLs

Topic What to know
Programmatic access Access keys for users, roles for compute; named profiles in the config files; never commit keys to code
Authenticated calls Requests are signed with SigV4 by the SDK using the resolved credentials
API Gateway authorizers IAM, Cognito user pool, or Lambda authorizer (custom logic)
Presigned URL (S3) A URL that carries a signature so anyone holding it can GET or PUT one object for a limited time, with the permissions of the signer
CloudFront signed URLs and cookies Time-limited access to private content at the edge
Exam tip

. "Let a user upload or download one private object without AWS credentials, for a limited time" = presigned URL. Its power ends when it expires or the signer's permission is lost.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A mobile app's users sign in and must then upload files directly to an S3 bucket using their own AWS permissions. Which combination fits?

  • ACognito user pool for sign-in and a Cognito identity pool for temporary credentials
  • BCreate IAM users for every app user and attach an S3 policy to each
  • CEmbed one shared access key in the app and rotate it each quarter
  • DMake the bucket public so that every signed-in user can upload
Show the answer

Answer: A. The user pool authenticates; the identity pool provides temporary credentials.

S2A backend must let a user download one private S3 object for ten minutes. What should it generate?

  • AA public bucket policy
  • BA new IAM user
  • CA presigned URL with a 10-minute expiry
  • DA KMS key
Show the answer

Answer: C. A presigned URL grants time-limited access to one object.

S3An application in account A must use a role in account B. Which API call provides temporary credentials?

  • Aiam:CreateUser
  • Bs3:GetObject
  • Csts:AssumeRole
  • Dkms:Decrypt
Show the answer

Answer: C. AssumeRole returns temporary credentials for the role.

S4A user policy allows s3:* but a bucket policy has an explicit deny for that user. What is the result?

  • AAllowed
  • BDenied
  • CAllowed only with MFA
  • DAllowed for reads only
Show the answer

Answer: B. An explicit deny always wins.

S5A Lambda function needs to call DynamoDB. What is the best way to grant access?

  • AAn execution role with a least-privilege policy
  • BEmbed access keys in the code
  • CUse the root user
  • DMake the table public
Show the answer

Answer: A. Roles provide temporary credentials and follow least privilege.

S6Employees must sign in to an AWS-integrated app with the company's SAML directory and receive temporary AWS access. What is this called?

  • AEncryption at rest
  • BCross-region replication
  • CResource tagging
  • DIdentity federation
Show the answer

Answer: D. Federation maps external identities to temporary AWS access.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What always wins in IAM policy evaluation?

Show the answer

An explicit deny.

R2What does a role's trust policy say?

Show the answer

Who may assume the role.

R3What does a Cognito user pool return?

Show the answer

JWT tokens (ID, access and refresh).

R4What does a Cognito identity pool provide?

Show the answer

Temporary AWS credentials.

R5Whose permissions does a presigned URL use?

Show the answer

The signer's.

R6Which service issues temporary credentials?

Show the answer

AWS STS.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
IAM default deny; explicit deny wins; roles for compute; least privilege
STS AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, AssumeRoleWithSAML; temporary credentials
Cognito user pool = sign-in and tokens; identity pool = AWS credentials
Presigned URL time-limited access to one object with the signer's permissions
